introduction.text: The Monument to the Cairoli Brothers is a prominent patriotic statuary group on the Pincian Hill in Rome, commemorating the sacrifice of the Cairoli brothers during the Italian unification.

history.description: Ernesto Cairoli was killed in 1859 at the Battle of Varese.
Luigi Cairoli fought in 1860 as part of the Expedition of the Thousand.
Enrico Cairoli was killed in 1867 at the Battle of Villa Glori.
A plaster model of the monument was exhibited in 1872 at the Fine Arts Exhibition of Rome.
The bronze monument was inaugurated on 27 May 1883.

design.description: The monument was designed by Ercole Rosa and depicts Giovanni Cairoli holding his wounded brother while defiantly raising a gun, with a base listing the names of 70 soldiers who fought at Villa Glori.

art.description: The arrangement of the two soldiers echoes the Hellenistic model of Menelaus supporting the body of Patroclus, creating a dramatic contrast between grief and defiance.
